chunks: And ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"What is between the hairline and the tip of the nose is a place of sajdah, so whatever part of it touches the ground has sufficed for you."

key_terms.أَجْزَأَكَ: it has been sufficient for you; it fulfills the requirement
key_terms.طَرَفِ: the end or tip of something
key_terms.قُصَاصِ: the hairline or edge where the hair begins
key_terms.مَسْجِدٌ: a place of sajdah; the area designated for prostration

ai.seo_question: What part of the face must touch the ground in sajdah for it to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the valid area of the face for sajdah. It states that the region from the hairline to the tip of the nose counts as the place of prostration, so contact of any part of that area with the ground is sufficient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.840 - Ammar al-Sabati narrate from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"The area between the hairline and the tip of the nose is considered a place of prostration (masjid), so whatever part of it touches the ground suffices."
